QuestionStmt.S: Identify the correct decreasing order of boiling points for different organic compounds from following.

Solution.S:
Concept: Boiling points of organic compounds depend on the strength of intermolecular forces, especially hydrogen bonding.

- Carboxylic acids have the strongest hydrogen bonding (they form dimers), giving them the highest boiling points.
- Alcohols have moderate hydrogen bonding, so their boiling points are lower than carboxylic acids but higher than amines.
- Amines have weaker hydrogen bonds compared to alcohols and carboxylic acids, so they have the lowest boiling points among the three.

Hence, the correct decreasing order is:

Carboxylic acids > Alcohols > Amines

This corresponds to option B.
